title: Creative
hired_for: To keep a steady supply of ads that stop the right shopper and sell, and to know which ideas win and why, so ad spend buys the most gross profit.

jobs.job: Tell me which ads are winning and losing, and why
jobs.why: Without a clear read, budget keeps flowing to ads that look busy but do not sell, and winners get cut too soon. Knowing why an ad wins tells the team what to make next.

watch.metric: share of spend on ads at or under the target cost per purchase, 7 days

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 45% of spend sits on ads above target. After: 70% on ads at or under target within 14 days, each winner and loser with a written reason.

jobs.job: Spot a tired ad before it burns budget, and tell a tired ad from an underfunded one
jobs.why: A worn out ad keeps spending while results slide. But an ad that only looks tired may just need more budget or a wider audience, and killing it throws away a winner.

watch.metric: click rate drop from the ad's own peak, and reach growth this 7 days against the prior 7
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad and ad set level

drives.metric: cost per purchase

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 3 of the top 5 ads have lost 30% of their click rate with flat reach. After: refreshed within 7 days; cost per purchase back under target.

jobs.job: Make sure each ad and its landing page argue the same thing
jobs.why: An ad that sells comfort and lands on a page about price loses the shopper at the click. The creative gets blamed for a page problem.

watch.metric: bounce rate on the landing page by ad, mobile, 7 days
watch.source: GA4 with ad tags, joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: conversion rate from ad clicks

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the best hook ad lands on the home page; bounce 72%. After: it lands on the matching product page; bounce 56%.
jobs.who_today: media buyer and designer, rarely together

jobs.job: Find hooks that stop the right viewer in the first 3 seconds
jobs.why: If the first 3 seconds do not stop the right person, nothing after matters. The hook is the cheapest part to change and moves results fastest.

watch.metric: hook rate (3 second views divided by impressions) against the account's own average, 7 days

drives.metric: click through rate and cost per purchase

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the median hook rate is 22%. After: 5 new hooks per winning ad; the median new hook at 29%.

jobs.job: Keep enough new ads coming each month to replace the ones that tire
jobs.why: Ads wear out. An account that runs on 2 or 3 old winners hits a wall when they fade, and costs jump.

watch.metric: new ads launched this month against plan
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and brand brain creative plan

drives.metric: share of new ads that become winners

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 6 new ads last month against a plan of 20. After: 20 a month, on time, with 4 net new ideas each month.

jobs.job: Keep a mix of ideas and formats so one ad does not carry the account
jobs.why: When one ad takes most of the spend, the account falls apart the day it tires. A mix of ideas reaches different shoppers and steadies cost.

watch.metric: share of spend on the top 3 ads, 7 days

drives.metric: week to week swing in cost per purchase

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the top 3 ads take 78% of spend. After: under 50%, spread across 5 ideas and 3 formats.

jobs.job: Revive a tired winner with new hooks before building from scratch
jobs.why: A proven body with a fresh opening often works again at a fraction of the cost of a new idea. It is the fastest way back to target.

watch.metric: cost per purchase of refreshed versions against the original ad's best 14 days

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the old winner runs at $41 per purchase against $26 at its peak. After: 4 new hooks; the best at $28.

jobs.job: Raise the share of new ads that become winners
jobs.why: Every ad costs money to make and to test. A better hit rate means less money spent on ads that never pay back.

watch.metric: new ads reaching the scale bar within 14 days of first spend, share, 90 days

drives.metric: cost per purchase

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 1 in 12 new ads reaches the bar. After: 1 in 7 within a quarter, with each brief built on a tested angle.

jobs.job: Turn customer words and reviews into angles worth testing
jobs.why: The best angles come from what buyers say in reviews and tickets, not from a brainstorm. Angles built on real words stop the right people.

watch.metric: live ads built on a sourced customer angle, share
watch.source: brand brain creative tags joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: share of new ads that become winners

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 3 of 20 live ads trace to a customer angle. After: 12 of 20.
jobs.who_today: creative strategist, if there is one

jobs.job: Keep viewers watching until the offer
jobs.why: A strong hook with a weak middle loses people before they see the product or the offer. Hold rate shows where they drop.

watch.metric: hold rate (full or 15 second views divided by 3 second views), 7 days

drives.metric: link click rate

jobs.now_after: Example: Now half of viewers leave by second 6. After: the product shows by second 4 in the recut; hold rate up from 18% to 25%.

jobs.job: Stop claims, fake scarcity or unlicensed faces from getting ads rejected or pulled
jobs.why: A rejected ad stops spend and a pattern of rejections can restrict the whole account. One bad claim can also bring legal trouble.

watch.metric: ads rejected or limited, count, 30 days

drives.metric: spend blocked by rejections

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 5 ads rejected last month for health claims. After: 0, with every claim checked against the brain before launch.

jobs.job: Get approved ads live within days, not weeks
jobs.why: An approved ad sitting in a folder is not selling. Long gaps between brief and launch mean tired ads run longer than they should.

watch.metric: days from brief to first spend, median, 90 days
watch.source: brand brain brief log joined to Meta first spend date

drives.metric: new ads launched per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 19 days from brief to first spend. After: 7 days.

jobs.job: Promote products we have in stock, not ones about to run out
jobs.why: Scaling an ad for a product with 2 weeks of stock sells out the winner and then wastes the audience. Slow stock needs its own push.

watch.metric: ad spend on products with under 30 days of stock, share, 7 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager joined to Shopify inventory

drives.metric: stockout days and days of stock

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 35% of spend is on a size bundle with 12 days of stock. After: under 10%; one ad made for the slowest selling line.
jobs.who_today: nobody; ads and stock are run by different people

jobs.job: Make catalog ads show the right price and badge on every product
jobs.why: Catalog ads pull from the product feed. A wrong price or a broken badge on some products shows up in thousands of ads at once.

watch.metric: products in the feed with errors or a broken price or badge, share

drives.metric: return on ad spend of catalog ads

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 9% of products in the feed have a price error. After: under 1%, checked after every feed sync.

jobs.job: Write a one page brief before any shoot or design so money is not wasted
jobs.why: Shoots and design work without a clear brief come back with pretty ads that argue nothing. The brief says who it is for, what it argues and how we will judge it.

watch.metric: live spend on ads with a brief on file, share, 30 days
watch.source: brand brain brief log joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: share of new ads that become winners

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 20% of live spend traces to a brief. After: 90%.

jobs.job: Show the real product in every ad so what arrives matches what was shown
jobs.why: AI images and heavy edits can redraw the product. When the item that arrives looks different, the customer returns it and leaves a bad review.

watch.metric: returns with reason not as pictured, share of orders from paid social, 60 days

drives.metric: return cost per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 2.1% of paid social orders come back as not as pictured. After: 1.0%, with real product photos in every ad.

jobs.job: Find and brief creators whose videos sell, not just get views
jobs.why: Creator videos with big view counts often sell little. Purchases per view shows who is worth briefing again.

watch.metric: purchases per 1,000 views on creator ads, 30 days

drives.metric: cost per purchase on creator ads

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 14 creators, 3 drive 80% of creator sales. After: the next batch briefed to the top 3 plus 3 new ones on the same brief.

jobs.job: Aim most new ads at people who do not know us yet
jobs.why: Most growth comes from shoppers who have never heard of the brand. Ads made for people who already know us look good in reports but add few new customers.

watch.metric: new ads aimed at cold shoppers, share of new ads, 30 days
watch.source: brand brain creative tags joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: cost per new customer

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 30% of new ads speak to cold shoppers. After: 70%.

jobs.job: Learn from every test so the next brief is better
jobs.why: If no one writes down why a winner won, the team cannot repeat it. The same mistakes cost money every month.

watch.metric: top and bottom spend ads with a written breakdown of why, share, 30 days
watch.source: brand brain creative notes joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: share of new ads that become winners

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 2 of the top 10 ads have a written reason. After: 10 of 10, each feeding the next brief.

jobs.job: Turn one approved ad into every size, caption and length without manual rework
jobs.why: Each placement needs its own size and captions. Doing it by hand delays launch and ads run in the wrong shape, which costs reach.

watch.metric: approved ads missing a size, caption or length 3 days after approval, count

drives.metric: placements covered per ad

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 8 approved ads lack a vertical version. After: 0 after 3 days.

jobs.job: Know what each finished ad costs to make and whether it paid back
jobs.why: Some ads cost $2,000 to shoot and never earn it back. Others cost $50 and carry the month. Without the cost, no one can judge.

watch.metric: cost per finished ad that reached live spend, monthly
watch.source: brand brain production cost log joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: production cost as a share of media spend

jobs.now_after: Example: Now no cost tracking. After: $310 per finished ad; video shoots at 4 times the cost of statics with the same hit rate.

jobs.job: Test new angles cheaply as still images before paying for video
jobs.why: Video costs more and takes longer. A still image shows in days whether an angle stops people, before money goes into a shoot.

watch.metric: angles tested as a still image before any video, share
watch.source: brand brain creative log joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: production cost as a share of media spend

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 4 of 5 new angles go straight to video. After: every new angle tested as a still first; 2 of 5 dropped before a shoot.

jobs.job: Track usage rights and creator permissions before they expire on live ads
jobs.why: An ad running after a music license or creator permission ends can be taken down or bring a claim. It is easy to track and costly to miss.

watch.metric: live ads with a right or permission ending in 30 days, count
watch.source: brand brain rights log joined to Meta ads

drives.metric: ads taken down for a rights claim

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 3 live ads use creator videos with permission ending in 2 weeks. After: renewed or replaced before the date.

jobs.job: Plan creative for the big dates early enough
jobs.why: Holiday and gifting ads made in the last week miss the start of the season. The best dates need ads ready and tested before demand peaks.

watch.metric: peak season ads ready 3 weeks before the date, share of plan

drives.metric: revenue in the peak window

jobs.now_after: Example: Now last year's holiday ads launched 5 days before the gifting deadline. After: 80% of holiday ads live 3 weeks ahead.

jobs.job: See what competitors are testing that we are not, as ideas, not answers
jobs.why: Competitor ads show formats and angles worth a test. They are not proof those ads work, and copying them is never allowed.

watch.metric: formats or angles run by 3 or more competitors that we have not tried in 90 days, count

drives.metric: share of new ads that become winners

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 4 open gaps, including side by side comparison ads. After: 2 tested in the next month with our own claims and footage.
